workflow: A diagnostic test launches a failing child process and expects its error output after termination.
The supervising display loop uses a fixed short sequence of polling events before requesting exit.
System load or execution instrumentation delays the child, so it has not finished when the fixed sequence ends.
The supervisor exits before collecting the child's diagnostics, leaving empty output and causing the test assertion to fail.
summary: Load-sensitive premature termination loses child diagnostics
decision_reason: The underlying failure is materially the same as the existing load-sensitive timeout cluster: a fixed timing assumption fails under slower scheduling, causing expected early results to be absent even though the operation itself remains valid.
